corrections.corrects: the claim that the port-8080 llama-server was an HCLI orphan, and the conclusion that no unowned model process remained
corrections.what_actually_happened: At 18:38 a llama-server on port 8080 (pid 6893) was killed on the assumption it was an orphan leaked by HCLI's RuntimePool. It was not. A server with the same signature (--host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --ctx-size 32768, no mmproj) reappeared at 18:48:27 as pid 10803, and its parent chain is `-zsh` <- `login -pf scammermike` <- Terminal.app — a HUMAN-OWNED interactive shell. It has 4 slots with 1 actively processing, so it is in use. The process killed at 18:38 was almost certainly the same operator-owned server, not an HCLI leak.
corrections.why_the_misattribution_happened: HCLI's RuntimePool spawns with start_new_session=True and its _command() shape is `--model X --port P --host 127.0.0.1 --ctx-size N`, which is very close to what the operator's server looked like. But HCLI allocates EPHEMERAL ports via allocate_port() (bind to port 0), so it can never produce port 8080. That single fact was available and would have refuted the orphan theory before the kill.
corrections.what_stands: The odyssey findings are unaffected and independently evidenced: odyssey_ctl.py DID leak its MLX patient runner, which reparented to PID 1 after its parents were terminated (observed directly as pid 5950 -> 6130). That is a real orphan-child defect. The port-8080 attribution is the part that was wrong.
corrections.policy_change: Model processes are no longer killed on inference. The probes now call foreign_model_load(), refuse to measure by default when a process they did not start is resident, and require an explicit --allow-foreign-load which records the co-tenant and its slot activity into the receipt. A contended measurement is now labelled a floor rather than a roof.
